definitions.gloss: heat-resistant; heatproof; able to withstand high temperatures
definitions.explanation: The property of being able to endure high temperatures without damage, deformation, or loss of function. Used for materials, containers, and products designed to resist heat.

examples.japanese: {耐熱|たいねつ}ガラスの{容器|ようき}を{使|つか}う。
このボウルは{耐熱|たいねつ}なので、{電子|でんし}レンジで{使|つか}える。
examples.english: This bowl is heat-resistant, so it can be used in the microwave.

examples.japanese: {耐熱|たいねつ}{温度|おんど}は200{度|ど}までとなっています。
examples.english: The heat-resistant temperature is up to 200 degrees.

notes:
A technical modifier meaning "heat-resistant." Functions as a prefix-like noun that modifies the following noun. Very common in product descriptions, cooking instructions, and materials science.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {耐熱|たいねつ}ガラス: heat-resistant glass (Pyrex-type)
- {耐熱|たいねつ}{容器|ようき}: heat-resistant container
- {耐熱|たいねつ}{温度|おんど}: heat-resistance temperature
- {耐熱|たいねつ}{素材|そざい}: heat-resistant material
- {耐熱|たいねつ}{皿|さら}: heat-resistant dish

FORMS:
Built with the prefix {耐|たい}〜 (resistance to ~), which combines with many nouns:
- {耐水|たいすい}: water-resistant
- {耐震|たいしん}: earthquake-resistant
- {耐久|たいきゅう}: durable, long-lasting

USAGE:
Commonly seen on product labels and in recipe instructions. {耐熱|たいねつ}{容器|ようき}に{入|い}れてレンジで{温|あたた}める (put in a heat-resistant container and microwave) is a standard instruction.
